title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
statement:
Given the `head` of a linked list, reverse the nodes of the list `k` at a time, and return the modified list.

`k` is a positive integer and is less than or equal to the length of the linked list. If the number of nodes is not a multiple of `k`, the nodes left over at the end should remain as they are.

You may not alter the values in the list's nodes, only the nodes themselves may be changed.

Build the list from `values`, reverse each group of `k` nodes in place (checking first that a full group of `k` nodes exists before reversing it), and return the resulting list as an array.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is n

editorial.approach: Use a dummy node before the head, with `groupPrev` tracking the node just before the current group. First, walk `k` nodes ahead from `groupPrev` to confirm a full group of `k` nodes exists (if not, stop — the remainder stays untouched). Reverse the group in place using the standard three-pointer technique, but link the reversed group's tail (the former first node) back to `groupPrev`, and set `groupPrev` to that tail. Advance to the next group and repeat until fewer than `k` nodes remain.
